strengths: The problem has an identifiable audience in binary analysis, software security, and representation learning. Constructing paired source code, LLVM representations, and generated summaries offers a practical approach to exploiting information available during pretraining.

Table VII contains promising binary-similarity results, particularly across substantially different compiler optimizations. For O0/O3 with a pool of 32, COMBO reports MRR of 0.436 versus GraphCodeBERT’s 0.376, despite using COMBO without downstream fine-tuning.
The diagrams communicate the intended training pipeline, and the breakdown across optimization pairs and retrieval-pool sizes reveals both improvements and settings where the advantage disappears.
weaknesses: Necessary—align the central claims with the evaluated inputs. The abstract and experimental questions promise binary vulnerability detection, but Section V-D explicitly evaluates source-code snippets. Pretraining and POJ-104 use LLVM IR, while BinaryCorp evaluates x86 disassembly. These experiments do not establish successful binary analysis across all three claimed tasks. Supply the missing binary vulnerability evaluation or consistently narrow the claims.

Necessary—resolve the POJ-104 evaluation protocol. Section IV-B and Table II specify disjoint training, development, and test problem classes (64/16/24), whereas Section V-B describes classification into 104 classes and reporting metrics across all 104. An ordinary supervised classifier cannot recognize classes absent from training without an additional mechanism. Specify whether this is classification or retrieval, explain how unseen classes are handled, and report the actual evaluation population and retained counts after compilation failures. Table VI is currently difficult to interpret reliably.

Necessary—support the claimed contributions of interpolation and gradual training. Table V compares minimum validation losses at successive stages that change the representation pairs and targets while adding training. Lower losses under these different objectives do not establish better representations or isolate a component’s contribution. COMBO versus COMBO-Light also changes training duration throughout. Controlled downstream ablations with comparable training budgets are needed to attribute improvements to interpolation, its schedule, or the comment modality; otherwise, restrict conclusions to the complete pipeline.

Necessary—make the method sufficiently specified to reproduce. Equation (4) omits the softmax described in the prose, leaving raw similarities as the cross-entropy targets in Equation (5). Clarify the implemented objective, normalization, and whether gradients pass through the targets. The encoder architectures and initializations, tokenization and sequence handling, and pretraining partition construction are also insufficiently specified. Referring to SimpleCLIP does not resolve these choices for code inputs.

Necessary—calibrate comparative claims and quantify uncertainty. The experiments compare against three text/source-code models, without evaluating the cited binary-code model jTrans. Broad superiority claims require relevant comparisons or narrower wording; achieving state-of-the-art performance is not itself necessary for publication. The different training schedules also limit causal interpretation. Single-seed results provide little evidence that small differences, such as POJ-104 F1 of 0.700 versus 0.696, are reliable.

Necessary—audit the numerical reporting and metric definitions. The headline 5.45% average improvement has no specified aggregation that makes it verifiable. Table V’s decrease from 0.048 to 0.039 is 18.75%, not the reported 25.6%. In Table VIII, every reported MicroF1 equals the arithmetic mean of the six displayed F1 values, while MacroF1 differs; the aggregation needs explanation. The vulnerability task also alternates between detecting vulnerable versus normal snippets and classifying already-vulnerable snippets by type. These ambiguities affect the substantive interpretation of the results.

Optional—a small audit of CodeT5-generated summaries and analysis of learned interpolation weights would help explain when the additional modality is useful. These would strengthen understanding, but the rejection rests on the claim–evidence mismatches and unresolved evaluation specifications above.
